la-palina--classic-natural.description: La Palina's Classic line, launched around 2012 as the brand's value range and reworked in 2017 with new wrapper versions, is rolled in the Dominican Republic. The Natural wears a light-brown Honduran leaf over a Honduran binder. Medium in strength and body, it moves from sweet cream and graham cracker through cedar, hay and salted nuts to caramel, baking spice and leather.

thirds.notes: Sweet and creamy at first, then graham cracker with vanilla, cinnamon, hay and a mild pepper.
Cedar and pepper stay prominent, with a mineral note, hay and creamy salted nuts.
A caramel-like sweetness, more baking spice, leather and nuts, with an earthy note late on.

sources.title: Blind Man's Puff – La Palina Classic Natural Toro review
Neptune Cigar – La Palina Classic Natural
Cigars Direct – La Palina Classic

la-palina--classic-maduro.description: The darkest of La Palina's four Classic blends, the Maduro pairs a dark Honduran maduro wrapper with a Honduran binder and long filler from Honduras, Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic. Medium to full in strength, it is built on bittersweet espresso, cocoa and leather with a lively spice and a creamy finish.

sources.title: Smoke Inn – La Palina Classic Maduro
Neptune Cigar – La Palina Classic Maduro Toro
Cigars Direct – La Palina Classic

la-palina--classic-rosado.description: The Classic Rosado belongs to La Palina's value Classic range and is made at General Cigar Dominicana, with a Honduran wrapper over a Honduran binder and filler from the Dominican Republic, Honduras and Nicaragua. Modest in strength but ample in body, it smokes smooth and cool, with wood, floral and herbal notes, minerals and a touch of dark cacao.

sources.title: Cigar Weekly – La Palina Classic Rosado
Cigars Direct – La Palina Classic

la-palina--black-label.description: Introduced at IPCPR 2014 as La Palina's seventh line and its second project with PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic, Black Label is the brand's bold blend: a dark Brazilian Bahiano wrapper over a double binder and filler of Dominican and Nicaraguan tobacco. Pepper, cocoa and oak open, coffee takes over midway, and nuts and cocoa close.

thirds.notes: Pepper, spice and cocoa up front, with oak and cedar, softening to sweet oak on the retrohale.
The pepper fades and a rich coffee takes the lead, with spice and oak still present.
Anise, toasted nuts and cocoa hold to the end, with coffee and leather in the background.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – La Palina Black Label Robusto review
Blind Man's Puff – La Palina Black Label review
Cigar.com – La Palina Black Label

la-palina--blue-label.description: Blue Label began as a limited La Palina release in a single toro and became a permanent line. It is rolled in Honduras at the Plasencia family's El Paraíso factory, with a Honduran Habano wrapper over a Habano binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Smooth and creamy with a gentle spice, it shows sweet cedar, leather and earth with a hint of orange peel.

sources.title: Cigars International – La Palina Blue Label
Neptune Cigar – La Palina Blue Label Robusto
Smoke Inn – La Palina Blue Label

la-palina--bronze-label.description: Bronze Label is a La Palina collaboration with Rocky Patel, first sold as a limited TAA release in 2017 and made a regular line in 2018. It is rolled at the Plasencia El Paraíso factory in Danlí, Honduras, with a Honduran Habano-seed wrapper, Honduran binder and Honduran and Nicaraguan filler. Medium in strength, it moves from coffee and cream to cedar, honey and nuts.

thirds.notes: Creamy coffee with a citrus sweetness and a peppery retrohale, then sweet cedar.
Cream and a caramel or honey sweetness lead, with nuts and cedar in balance.
Pepper and spice build over nutty, savory notes, and leather grows towards the end.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – La Palina Bronze Label Robusto review
Blind Man's Puff – La Palina Bronze Label Robusto review

la-palina--el-diario.description: El Diario, Spanish for 'The Daily', was conceived as an everyday offshoot of La Palina. It is hand-made in Honduras with a Honduran Corojo rosado wrapper, a Honduran Criollo binder and Criollo and Corojo filler. A full-bodied smoke, it opens with white pepper, toasted nuts and hints of chocolate, cedar and leather, then lets leather and nuts lead.

thirds.notes: A white-pepper kick, then a toasty profile of nuts and more pepper, with traces of chocolate, cedar and leather.
Leather and nuts move to the front.
The profile holds steady while the body grows noticeably heavier.

sources.title: Cigar Inspector – La Palina El Diario Gordo review
Cigar Place – La Palina El Diario

la-palina--el-ano-1896.description: El Año 1896, a nod to the year La Palina was first made, is the brand's first box-pressed cigar: a dark Mexican San Andrés oscuro wrapper over a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, made by PDR Cigars in the Dominican Republic. Medium to full, it brings red pepper, chocolate, espresso and a savory, meaty side.

thirds.notes: Spicy red pepper with chocolate, cream, espresso, cedar and roasted nuts, turning savory and malty.
Red pepper returns and the earlier flavors come back without fully coming together.
Black pepper and noticeable nicotine take over as the flavors come and go.

sources.title: Smoke Inn – La Palina El Año 1896
Kohnhed – La Palina El Año 1896 Oscuro review
